title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط السادس تابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape six, continued
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين، أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: "ثم الطعن إما أن يكون لكذب الراوي أو تهمته بذلك أو فحش غلطه أو غفلته أو فسقه أو وهمه أو مخالفته أو جهالته أو بدعته أو سوء حفظه" فذكر هنا هذه الأقسام من أقسام الطعن على حسب ترتيبه هو، وهو يختلف عن الترتيب الذي عليه جمهور أهل المصطلح، وهو الترتيب الذي سقناه سابقا، فتكون الأقسام به أقل من هذا التقسيم، لأن هذا التقسيم بعضه يشترك في الاسم، فذكره مع كونه مشتركا في الاسم كأقسام مما يزيد العدد من غير كبير فائدة، فلذلك لم ننتهج هذا لكن لا بأس بشرحه، فهنا قال إن الطعن، له أسباب السبب الأول أن يكون لكذب الراوي أي أن يكون الراوي معروفا بالكذب وذلك بإقراره هو..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and all his Companions.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "Then the impugning of a narrator is either for the narrator's lying, or for his being suspected of it, or for the grossness of his error, or for his heedlessness, or for his open transgression, or for his misapprehension, or for his contradicting [others], or for his being unknown, or for his innovation, or for his poor retention." He mentioned here these divisions among the divisions of impugning, according to his own arrangement, which differs from the arrangement followed by the majority of the people of the terminology — the arrangement which we set out earlier. The divisions on that arrangement are fewer than on this division, because some parts of this division share a single name; so his mentioning them, while they share a name, as separate divisions, is of the sort that increases the number without great benefit. For that reason we did not follow this, though there is no harm in explaining it. Here, then, he said that impugning has causes. The first cause is the narrator's lying, that is, that the narrator is known for lying, and that by his own admission..

flags.context: the heading of the whole passage
flags.note: Ṭaʿn is the technical act of stating a ground on which a narrator's reports are not to be accepted; it is the negative half of al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, which the glossary fixes as 'the appraisal of narrators'. 'Criticism' is too weak and too general, and 'disparagement' imports a moral charge that some of the ten grounds listed — heedlessness, poor retention, being unknown — do not carry at all. The word should be added to the glossary.

flags.context: the sixth and tenth of the ten grounds of impugning
flags.note: Two of the ten grounds are easily collapsed into each other or into the third ground, 'the grossness of his error' (fuḥsh ghalaṭihi), in English. Wahm is a narrator's forming a mistaken impression of what he heard; sūʾ al-ḥifẓ is unreliability in retaining it; ghalaṭ is plain error. The Sheikh's whole complaint against Ibn Hajar's arrangement is precisely that some of these grounds share a name, so the English must keep the ten distinguishable or the criticism becomes unintelligible.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. This record is the second half of tape six; the first half does not appear anywhere in the range 601–652. The series as held in this range is therefore incomplete — see the third flag.

The Sheikh is criticising Ibn Hajar's arrangement of the grounds of impugning, not the grounds themselves, and he expressly says he taught a different arrangement earlier and will nevertheless explain this one. That distinction has been kept visible; nothing in the passage should be read as his rejecting any of the ten grounds.
'Open transgression' renders fisq, as at id 608.
The quoted matn is Ibn Hajar's, and its bare enumeration has not been smoothed into English prose.
